note: No screenshots in this lesson -- documented here honestly rather than silently defaulting to code/steps. Before writing this lesson, docs.aws.amazon.com's current IAM User Guide pages were checked directly for real UI screenshots across multiple pages (id_users_create.html, tutorial_managed-policies.html, getting-started-account-iam.html, and the MediaConvert and Control Tower guides' IAM-adjacent pages) using both curl and the browser tool with network-request and DOM img-tag inspection. Every page returned zero screenshot images -- only the AWS logo SVG and (on one page) internal recommendation-beacon tracking pixels, confirmed via `Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('img')).map(img => img.src))` in the browser console. AWS's current docs platform does not appear to render console screenshots on these pages at all (a platform-wide change, not something specific to IAM). A 2017 AWS Security Blog post about the IAM console does have screenshots, but its role-creation wizard is years out of date and would misrepresent the current console, so it was not used. Rather than fabricate or use stale/misleading imagery, this lesson uses real, correct IAM policy JSON (an S3 read-only identity-based policy and a role trust policy, both verified against AWS's own policy-elements and AssumeRole documentation) on code slides, consistent with SCREENSHOTS.md's guidance that a lesson without genuine real UI to show should fall back to an honest code card rather than pad with an unrelated or fabricated screenshot.
